subject: System Design
title: NoSQL at Scale
description: A quick, practical guide to NoSQL at Scale.

hook.text: Cassandra handles 1 million writes per second across hundreds of nodes. How does it manage that?

buildup.text: NoSQL databases like Cassandra and DynamoDB are designed for horizontal scaling from the ground up.

discovery.text: They use consistent hashing to distribute data across nodes without a central coordinator.

twist.text: The trade-off: no JOINs, limited transactions, and you must design your schema around your queries.

climax.text: NoSQL at scale is powerful but demands a query-first mindset that feels alien to SQL developers.

punchline.text: Design your tables for your queries, not your data.

quiz.question: How do NoSQL databases like Cassandra distribute data?
